title: Instance rate limits are directional: inflows are capped while outflows are left unlimited
content:
Instance Configuration Documents carry separate inflow and outflow limits. For the SparkLend USDS Instance, A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.3.1.1.1.2.4.1 sets inflow at `maxAmount`: 200,000,000 USDS with `slope`: 400,000,000 USDS per day, while A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.3.1.1.1.2.4.2 sets outflow to `maxAmount`: Unlimited, `slope`: Unlimited.

The asymmetry is the design. Building exposure to a venue is throttled; unwinding it is not. That is the correct direction for a risk control — a limit exists to bound how fast risk can be taken on, and a limit on exit would bound how fast risk can be shed, which is the opposite of what a risk control should do.

It is the same pattern that appears at the global level, where reversing an operation credits the forward limit rather than consuming a separate one, and it is what makes the pre-written emergency wind-down executable in a single pass at full balance.

The inflow numbers show a second choice: `slope` (400M/day) exceeds `maxAmount` (200M), so the bucket refills fully in half a day. The instantaneous cap is doing the real work — bounding any single move to 200M — while sustained daily throughput is deliberately generous. Read together, the parameters say: no large sudden concentration into one venue, but no meaningful friction on steady rebalancing, and no friction at all on getting out.
description: The SparkLend USDS Instance permits 200M USDS inflow with a 400M/day slope but Unlimited outflow — the same easy-to-exit asymmetry the global limits use, applied per venue.
